category: SerDes Toolbox, Signal Integrity Toolbox & Mixed-Signal Blockset > Equalizers, Channels, Eye Analysis & Delta-Sigma Design
description: MATLAB-level functions and System objects of SerDes Toolbox (CTLE, FFE, DFE/CDR, AGC, channel loss models, stimulus, statistical eye and pulse-response analysis, SerDes Designer), Signal Integrity Toolbox (TDR, link designer apps) and Mixed-Signal Blockset (delta-sigma modulator synthesis, realization and simulation, SNR analysis, Mixed-Signal Analyzer). Only names confirmed in the MathWorks reference pages are included.

tools.name: serdes.CTLE
tools.description: System object modeling a continuous-time linear equalizer (peaking filter) for SerDes receivers or transmitters, specified by DC gain/peaking gain/peaking frequency or explicit gain-pole-zero data, with fixed or adaptive configuration selection.
tools.usage:
ctle = serdes.CTLE
ctle = serdes.CTLE(Name, Value)
y = ctle(x)

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description: 0 off, 1 fixed, 2 adapt (default) - adapt selects the best configuration.

parameters.name: Specification
parameters.description: E.g. "DC Gain and Peaking Gain" (default), "DC Gain and AC Gain", "AC Gain and Peaking Gain", "GPZ Matrix".

parameters.name: DCGain / PeakingGain / PeakingFrequency / GPZ
parameters.description: Response definition vectors (one entry per configuration).

tools.notes: The CTLE Fitter app fits pole/zero models to measured transfer functions. Blocks with the same names exist for Simulink SerDes systems.

tools.name: serdes.FFE
tools.description: System object modeling a feed-forward equalizer (FIR tap filter), typically used as transmitter de-emphasis/pre-emphasis in serial links, with fixed or adaptive tap weights and optional normalization.
tools.usage:
ffe = serdes.FFE
ffe = serdes.FFE(Name, Value)
y = ffe(x)

parameters.name: TapWeights
parameters.description: Tap weights including the main cursor, e.g. [-0.1 0.8 -0.1].

parameters.name: Normalize
parameters.description: Normalize taps so their absolute sum equals 1.

tools.notes: Pair with serdes.ChannelLoss and a receive CTLE/DFE to optimize link equalization.

tools.name: serdes.DFE
tools.description: System object modeling a decision feedback equalizer that cancels post-cursor intersymbol interference at clock sampling times, with fixed or LMS-adaptive tap weights and tap limits.
tools.usage:
dfe = serdes.DFE
dfe = serdes.DFE(Name, Value)
[y, TapWeights] = dfe(x)
tools.notes: serdes.DFECDR combines the DFE with clock and data recovery for time-domain (sample) simulation.

tools.name: serdes.DFECDR
tools.description: System object combining a decision feedback equalizer with a clock and data recovery loop, adapting tap weights and sampling phase from the received waveform during bit-by-bit (time-domain) simulation.
tools.usage:
dfecdr = serdes.DFECDR
dfecdr = serdes.DFECDR(Name, Value)
[y, TapWeights, Phase] = dfecdr(x)
tools.notes: Sample-by-sample processing is slow in MATLAB; use the Simulink model exported from SerDes Designer for long simulations.

tools.name: serdes.AGC
tools.description: System object implementing automatic gain control that scales the signal toward a target RMS voltage, compensating channel loss ahead of equalizers.
tools.usage:
agc = serdes.AGC(Name, Value)
y = agc(x)

parameters.name: TargetRMSVoltage / AveragingLength / MaxGain
parameters.description: Target amplitude, averaging window and gain limit.

tools.example:
agc = serdes.AGC("TargetRMSVoltage", 0.4, "MaxGain", 5, "WaveType", "Sample");
y = arrayfun(@(s) agc(s), x);
tools.notes: serdes.VGA applies a fixed or selectable gain instead.

tools.name: serdes.VGA
tools.description: System object modeling a variable gain amplifier with a fixed gain (or mode off), used to set signal levels in SerDes transmit/receive chains.
tools.usage:
vga = serdes.VGA(Name, Value)
y = vga(x)
tools.example:
vga = serdes.VGA("Gain", 1.5, "Mode", 1);
y = vga(x);
tools.notes: Combine with serdes.SaturatingAmplifier to model output limiting.

tools.name: serdes.SaturatingAmplifier
tools.description: System object modeling a saturating (limiting) amplifier with linear gain, output limit and optional frequency response, capturing nonlinear compression in SerDes front ends.
tools.usage:
satAmp = serdes.SaturatingAmplifier(Name, Value)
y = satAmp(x)

parameters.name: Limit / LinearGain
parameters.description: Output voltage limit and small-signal gain.

parameters.name: Specification
parameters.description: How the response is specified (limit and gain, or with VI/transfer data).

tools.notes: Nonlinear blocks invalidate purely statistical (LTI) analysis; use time-domain simulation.

tools.name: serdes.ChannelLoss
tools.description: System object creating a simple lossy transmission line channel model from insertion loss at a target frequency, characteristic impedance and Tx/Rx termination parasitics, producing an impulse response for link analysis.
tools.usage:
channel = serdes.ChannelLoss(Name, Value)
impulse = channel.impulse

parameters.name: Loss / TargetFrequency
parameters.description: Insertion loss (dB) at the target (typically Nyquist) frequency.

parameters.name: dt
parameters.description: Sample interval of the impulse response.

tools.notes: For measured channels use S-parameters with SParameterChannel or the S-Parameter Fitter app.

tools.name: serdes.Stimulus
tools.description: System object generating a SerDes stimulus waveform sample by sample: PRBS or custom symbol patterns with NRZ/PAM-n modulation and optional random/deterministic jitter.
tools.usage:
stim = serdes.Stimulus(Name, Value)
sample = stim()

parameters.name: Order / Seed / SymbolPattern
parameters.description: PRBS order and seed or custom pattern.

tools.notes: prbs generates raw PRBS bit sequences; pulse2wave builds waveforms from pulse responses.

tools.name: eyeDiagramSI
tools.description: System object that builds eye diagrams from time-domain waveforms for signal-integrity analysis and measures eye height, width, area, levels, crossings, linearity, COM, VEC and jitter-related quantities.
tools.usage:
eyeObj = eyeDiagramSI(Name=Value)
eyeObj(waveform)
h = eyeHeight(eyeObj)
w = eyeWidth(eyeObj)
plot(eyeObj)

parameters.name: SampleInterval / SymbolTime
parameters.description: Waveform sample interval and unit interval.

parameters.name: Modulation
parameters.description: Number of levels (2 for NRZ, 4 for PAM4, ...).

tools.notes: Other measurement methods: eyeArea, eyeAmplitude, eyeLevels, eyeCrossing, eyeCenter, eyeLinearity, com, vec, risetime, falltime, margin (with eye masks).

tools.name: optPulseMetric
tools.description: Computes eye metrics (maximum and center eye height, eye width, eye area, COM, SNR) directly from a pulse response at a target bit error rate, providing a fast objective for optimizing equalizer settings.
tools.usage: metric = optPulseMetric(P, N, dt, B)
tools.notes: If the eye is closed at the target BER, the function increases the BER and reports it in usedBER. NRZ only.

tools.name: prbs
tools.description: Generates a pseudorandom binary sequence from a linear feedback shift register of a given order (or polynomial), returning the bits and final seed for continuing the sequence.
tools.usage:
[seq, seed] = prbs(O, N)
[seq, seed] = prbs(O, N, seed)

parameters.name: O
parameters.description: PRBS order (e.g. 7, 9, 15, 23, 31) or polynomial exponent vector.

parameters.name: seed
parameters.description: Initial register state to continue a sequence.

tools.notes: Communications Toolbox comm.PNSequence offers similar functionality with more polynomial options.

tools.name: impulse2pulse
tools.description: Converts an impulse response into a pulse (single-bit) response by convolving with a rectangular pulse of one symbol duration; the pulse response is the basis of statistical link analysis.
tools.usage: pulse = impulse2pulse(impulse, N, dt)

parameters.name: impulse
parameters.description: Impulse response column vector (or matrix for crosstalk).

tools.example:
pulse = impulse2pulse(channel.impulse, 16, 6.25e-12);
plot(pulse)
tools.notes: Related conversions: impulse2step, step2impulse, pulse2impulse, wave2pulse.

tools.name: pulse2stateye
tools.description: Generates a statistical eye diagram from a pulse response (and optional crosstalk pulses) using the Hula-Hoop algorithm, giving the probability distribution of the received eye without long time-domain simulation.
tools.usage:
[S, VH, TH] = pulse2stateye(P, N, M)
[S, VH, TH] = pulse2stateye(P, N, M, ClockIndex)
[___, S1] = pulse2stateye(P, N, M)
tools.notes: Without outputs it plots the eye. pulse2pda computes a peak-distortion-analysis eye.

tools.name: pulse2wave
tools.description: Builds a time-domain data waveform by superposing shifted pulse responses according to a symbol pattern, a fast way to generate received waveforms of LTI links.
tools.usage: wave = pulse2wave(pulse, pattern, N)

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: Symbol pattern (e.g. PRBS bits or PAM levels).

tools.notes: The waveform is periodic with the pattern; wave2pulse extracts the pulse from a measured periodic waveform.

tools.name: serdesDesigner
tools.description: Opens the SerDes Designer app for designing serial links: configure transmitter/receiver equalization blocks (FFE, CTLE, DFE/CDR, AGC, VGA), channel loss or S-parameters, run statistical analysis with eye, bathtub and COM results, and export to Simulink, MATLAB or IBIS-AMI models.
tools.usage:
serdesDesigner
serdesDesigner(sessionFile)
tools.example: serdesDesigner   % then Export > Simulink model for time-domain simulation
tools.notes: Exported Simulink models can generate IBIS-AMI executables for EDA tools. IBIS Designer, S-Parameter Fitter and CTLE Fitter are companion apps.

tools.name: tdr
tools.description: Computes time-domain reflectometry responses from S-parameters to characterize impedance discontinuities along interconnects (connectors, vias, traces), in impedance or voltage form, for single-ended or differential ports.
tools.usage:
tdrObj = tdr(sparam)
tdrObj = tdr(sparam, Name=Value)
plot(tdrObj)
tools.notes: Read-only results: ImpedanceTDR, VoltageTDR, Time. tdr.sParamQuality reports passivity/causality/reciprocity metrics of the data.

tools.name: serialLinkDesigner
tools.description: Opens the Serial Link Designer app (Signal Integrity Toolbox) for system-level design and analysis of multi-gigabit serial links with IBIS-AMI models, channel topologies, statistical and time-domain simulation sweeps and compliance reporting.
tools.usage:
serialLinkDesigner
serialLinkDesigner(interfaceFile)
h = serialLinkDesigner(scriptFile)

parameters.name: scriptFile
parameters.description: Script file to run in batch; returns the app process handle.

tools.example: serialLinkDesigner   % create a project, add Tx/Rx IBIS-AMI models and channel, run sweeps
tools.notes: Results are explored in the Signal Integrity Viewer. Signal Integrity Kits provide preconfigured projects for standards such as PCIe and Ethernet.

tools.name: parallelLinkDesigner
tools.description: Opens the Parallel Link Designer app (Signal Integrity Toolbox) for analyzing parallel interfaces such as DDR memory buses: IBIS buffer models, topologies, timing budgets, crosstalk and simultaneous switching effects.
tools.usage:
parallelLinkDesigner
parallelLinkDesigner(interfaceFile)
h = parallelLinkDesigner(scriptFile)

parameters.name: scriptFile
parameters.description: Script file to run; returns the app process handle.

tools.example: parallelLinkDesigner   % open a DDR kit project and run a sweep
tools.notes: Uses the same Signal Integrity Viewer for waveform and report analysis as Serial Link Designer.

tools.name: synthesizeNTF
tools.description: Synthesizes the noise transfer function (NTF) of a delta-sigma modulator for a given order, oversampling ratio, zero optimization, maximum out-of-band gain and center frequency, returning a zpk model.
tools.usage: ntf = synthesizeNTF(order, osr, opt, H_inf, f0)

parameters.name: opt
parameters.description: Zero optimization: 0 none, 1 (optimized), 2, 3 (Optimization Toolbox) or 'z' with specified zeros.

parameters.name: H_inf / f0
parameters.description: Maximum out-of-band gain (Lee's rule: < 2 for binary quantizers) and normalized center frequency (0 for lowpass).

tools.notes: Mixed-Signal Blockset adopts the Delta-Sigma Toolbox API: realizeNTF, stuffABCD, scaleABCD, mapABCD, calculateTF, simulateDSM, simulateSNR, calculateSNR, predictSNR.

tools.name: realizeNTF
tools.description: Computes the coefficients (a, g, b, c) of a delta-sigma modulator loop-filter topology (e.g. CIFB, CIFF, CRFB, CRFF) that realizes a given NTF (and optional STF).
tools.usage:
[a, g, b, c] = realizeNTF(ntf)
[a, g, b, c] = realizeNTF(ntf, form)
[a, g, b, c] = realizeNTF(ntf, form, stf)
tools.notes: Scale state swings with scaleABCD, then map back with mapABCD to obtain implementable coefficients.

tools.name: stuffABCD
tools.description: Builds the ABCD state-space matrix of a delta-sigma modulator from topology coefficients (a, g, b, c) and structure name, for simulation and scaling.
tools.usage: ABCD = stuffABCD(a, g, b, c, form)

parameters.name: a, g, b, c
parameters.description: Feedback/feedforward, resonator, input and inter-stage coefficients.

tools.example:
ABCD = stuffABCD(a, g, b, c, "CIFB");
[ntf, stf] = calculateTF(ABCD);
tools.notes: mapABCD performs the inverse mapping from ABCD back to coefficients.

tools.name: scaleABCD
tools.description: Scales a delta-sigma modulator ABCD matrix so that internal state maxima stay below specified limits (dynamic range scaling), simulating the modulator to find state swings and the maximum stable input.
tools.usage: [ABCDs, umax, S] = scaleABCD(ABCD, nlev, f, xlim, ymax, umax, N, N0)

parameters.name: xlim / ymax / umax
parameters.description: State limits, quantizer input stability threshold, maximum input.

parameters.name: N / N0
parameters.description: Simulation length and number of initial samples ignored.

tools.example:
[ABCDs, umax] = scaleABCD(ABCD, 2, 0, 1);
[a, g, b, c] = mapABCD(ABCDs, "CIFB");
tools.notes: Returned umax is the maximum stable input amplitude relative to full scale.

tools.name: mapABCD
tools.description: Calculates loop-filter coefficients (a, g, b, c) for a specified modulator topology from an ABCD matrix, typically after scaling with scaleABCD.
tools.usage: [a, g, b, c] = mapABCD(ABCD, form)
tools.example:
[a, g, b, c] = mapABCD(ABCDs, "CIFB");
disp(a)
tools.notes: Use the coefficients to parameterize Mixed-Signal Blockset delta-sigma ADC models.

tools.name: calculateTF
tools.description: Computes the noise and signal transfer functions (NTF and STF) of a delta-sigma modulator described by an ABCD matrix and quantizer gain.
tools.usage:
[ntf, stf] = calculateTF(ABCD)
[ntf, stf] = calculateTF(ABCD, k)
tools.example:
[ntf2, stf2] = calculateTF(ABCDs);
bode(ntf2)
tools.notes: Verifies that a realized topology reproduces the designed NTF.

tools.name: simulateDSM
tools.description: Simulates a delta-sigma modulator (given by NTF or ABCD matrix) with a given input, returning the quantizer output, final and maximum states and quantizer input.
tools.usage:
[v, xn, xmax, y] = simulateDSM(u, ABCD)
[v, xn, xmax, y] = simulateDSM(u, ntf, nlev, x0)

parameters.name: u
parameters.description: Input signal (normalized to quantizer full scale).

tools.notes: calculateSNR computes SNR from the in-band FFT bins; simulateSNR sweeps input amplitudes.

tools.name: calculateSNR
tools.description: Calculates the signal-to-noise ratio from the in-band bins of a windowed FFT, given the bin index of the input tone and the number of signal bins, as used to evaluate delta-sigma modulator and ADC performance.
tools.usage:
snr = calculateSNR(hwfft, f)
snr = calculateSNR(hwfft, f, nsig)

parameters.name: hwfft
parameters.description: FFT of the Hann-windowed output (in-band portion).

parameters.name: f
parameters.description: Bin index of the signal tone.

parameters.name: nsig
parameters.description: Number of bins on each side of f counted as signal (default 1).

tools.example:
spec = fft(v .* hann(N)');
snr = calculateSNR(spec(1:fB), ftest)
tools.notes: Uses the Delta-Sigma Toolbox convention of 1-based bin indices relative to the provided spectrum.

tools.name: predictSNR
tools.description: Predicts the SNR versus input amplitude of a binary delta-sigma modulator from its NTF using the describing-function method, without time-domain simulation.
tools.usage:
[snr, amp, k0, k1, sigma_e2] = predictSNR(ntf, osr)
[snr, amp] = predictSNR(ntf, osr, amp, f0)

parameters.name: ntf / osr
parameters.description: Noise transfer function and oversampling ratio.

tools.notes: Applies to binary (2-level) quantizers; compare with simulateSNR for multi-bit designs.

tools.name: simulateSNR
tools.description: Determines SNR versus input amplitude of a delta-sigma modulator by time-domain simulation over a range of input levels, returning the SNR curve used to find peak SNR and dynamic range.
tools.usage:
[snr, amp] = simulateSNR(arg1, osr)
[snr, amp] = simulateSNR(arg1, osr, amp, f0, nlev, f, k)

parameters.name: amp / f0 / nlev / f / k
parameters.description: Input amplitudes (dBFS), center frequency, quantizer levels, test frequency and log2 FFT length.

tools.example:
[snr, amp] = simulateSNR(ntf, 64, -100:5:0);
[peakSNR, idx] = max(snr)
tools.notes: Slower than predictSNR but valid for multi-level quantizers and any topology.

tools.name: mixedSignalAnalyzer
tools.description: Opens the Mixed-Signal Analyzer app for importing and analyzing circuit simulation results (e.g. from Cadence Virtuoso ADE exports) of mixed-signal systems: plotting waveforms across corners and sweeps, computing metrics and building behavioral model data.
tools.usage:
mixedSignalAnalyzer
mixedSignalAnalyzer(fileName)

parameters.name: fileName
parameters.description: Simulation data file (.csv, .xlsx or .mat) to load at startup.

tools.example: mixedSignalAnalyzer   % then import a simulation database and create plots/metrics
tools.notes: Part of Mixed-Signal Blockset. adeinfo2msa extracts Cadence Virtuoso ADE results for the app; sessions can be exported as MATLAB scripts.
